name: Dagba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Glottolog refs (Keegan 2012 Eastern Sara Languages; Saragaza & Keegan, Lexique Daba, morkegbooks PDF read) — tonal lexicon, no stress statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 19th ed. (2016), entry Dagba [dgk] (Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: Demography/location only: 34,000 in CAR (Ouham: Batangafo, Kabo, Bossangoa), 10,000 in Chad (Grande Sido; Sarh); dialects none known; may be intelligible of Kabba [ksp].

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2006. Présentation des langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes (Lexique comparatif historique des langues SBB, LLACAN).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level presentation; a full-text search for stress/accent finds no Dagba/Daba entry and no accent/stress statement (only 'disparités lexicales accentuées').

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. [1989 data]. The Daba Language (synopsis of 1989 field notes from Gradjim Gobeti, Maikongo, south of Moissala, Chad; = 'Keegan 1989: Daba Word List. Ms.'). Morkeg Books, Sara-Bagirmi Language Project. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2 Phonological Notes, p. 1: inventory as Eastern Sara; on CVCV stems (tìbì, kòsó, känjä) 'the second vowel in each of these cases is pronounced markedly weaker than the first'; vowel length only in monosyllables. No use of the term stress/accent; the remark concerns vowel neutralization, not a stress rule.

sources.citation: Chabrelie, Louis. 1935. Notes sur la langue des Sara, avec un vocabulaire comparatif des différents dialectes. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 5(2): 125-151.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only pre-Keegan description that explicitly includes Dagba among the compared Sara dialects; the introductory 'notes sur la langue' may contain a colonial-era remark on accent/tone. Only p. 125 opening visible; Persée PDF blocked by bot-check by automated download (open on Persée in a browser).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. Extended Bibliography, Sara-Bagirmi Language Project. 7 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only Daba-specific item is Keegan 1989 'Daba Word List. Ms.'; the Eastern Sara volume's bibliography adds Saragaza, Sayam Ruth 1988 'Lo Ndo Ta Dagba' (Bibles International; primer/texts).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Eastern Sara Languages, 8th ed. (April 2014). Cuenca: Morkeg Books, The Sara Language Project. 454 pp. (= Glottolog 311667, 2012 2nd ed.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' p. 10 (PDF p. 14): 'All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low'; 'Introduction to the Daba Lexicon: Comments on the Phonology' pp. 23-26 (PDF pp. 27-30): word-final obstruents with prominent delayed release (fn. 21), no barred-i, no schwa, non-initial implosive. 'stress' 0 hits in 454 pp; no statement on word stress or accent.

sources.citation: Saragaza, Serge & John M. Keegan. 2014. Lexique Daba, 3e édition (avril 2014). Cuenca: Morkeg Books, The Sara Language Project. 68 pp. (= Glottolog 300413, 2011 ms. ed.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: One-page introduction (language, speaker, data collection); lexicon fully tone-marked H/M/L; the words stress / accent tonique / intensité do not occur. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Moéhama, Elisée. 2021. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: Première évaluation parmi les Dagba. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-003, 1-31. Dallas: SIL International.
